events.title: Electrical Conduction Discovered
events.description: Stephen Gray discovers that electricity can be conducted over long distances through wire.

events.title: Two-Mile Charge Experiment
events.description: Dr. William Watson sends an electric charge through two miles of wire, suggesting its use for messaging.

events.title: Electrostatic Telegraph Proposal
events.description: An anonymous writer 'C.M.' proposes an electrostatic telegraph in Scots Magazine.

events.title: Optical Telegraph Demonstration
events.description: Claude Chappe demonstrates the first 'Optical Telegraph' (semaphore) system in France.

events.title: First Commercial Semaphore Line
events.description: The first commercial semaphore line opens between Paris and Lille.

events.title: Invention of the Voltaic Pile
events.description: Alessandro Volta invents the Voltaic Pile, the first reliable chemical battery.

events.title: Electrochemical Telegraph Proposal
events.description: Francisco Salva Campillo proposes an electrochemical telegraph using bubbles in water.

events.title: Soemmering's Telegraph
events.description: Samuel Soemmering builds an electrochemical telegraph in Bavaria.

events.title: Ronalds' Electrostatic Telegraph
events.description: Francis Ronalds builds an electrostatic telegraph; the British Admiralty rejects it as 'unnecessary'.

events.title: Magnetic Field Discovery
events.description: Hans Christian Ørsted discovers that electric current creates a magnetic field.

events.title: Needle Telegraph Proposal
events.description: André-Marie Ampère proposes an electromagnetic telegraph using magnetized needles.

events.title: Schilling's Needle Telegraph
events.description: Baron Schilling develops the first electromagnetic needle telegraph in Russia.

events.title: Invention of the Electromagnet
events.description: William Sturgeon invents the electromagnet, the core component of the future telegraph.

events.title: Henry Rings a Bell
events.description: Joseph Henry rings a bell at a distance using an electromagnet and a mile of wire.

events.title: Morse's Telegraph Concept
events.description: Samuel Morse conceives the idea of an electromagnetic telegraph while on the ship Sully.

events.title: Gauss and Weber Telegraph
events.description: Gauss and Weber build a working electromagnetic telegraph in Göttingen, Germany.

events.title: Morse's First Prototype
events.description: Samuel Morse builds his first prototype using a wooden picture frame and a lead pencil.

events.title: Telegraph Relay Added
events.description: Morse adds a 'relay' to his system, allowing signals to travel long distances without fading.

events.title: Five-Needle Telegraph Patent
events.description: William Cooke and Charles Wheatstone patent the five-needle telegraph in England.

events.title: Demonstration to Leonard Gale
events.description: Samuel Morse demonstrates his telegraph to Professor Leonard Gale at NYU.

events.title: Alfred Vail Joins Morse
events.description: Alfred Vail joins Morse, bringing financial backing and crucial mechanical skill to the project.

events.title: Earth Ground Return Discovered
events.description: Carl August von Steinheil discovers that the earth can act as a 'ground return' for a circuit.

events.title: First Public Demonstration
events.description: First public demonstration of the Morse telegraph at Speedwell Ironworks, NJ.

events.title: Dots and Dashes Developed
events.description: Morse and Vail develop the 'dots and dashes' code, initially as a number-based dictionary.

events.title: Franklin Institute Demo
events.description: Morse demonstrates the telegraph to the Franklin Institute and President Martin Van Buren.

events.title: First Commercial Telegraph
events.description: The first commercial telegraph line in the world opens between Paddington and West Drayton, UK.

events.title: Morse's First US Patent
events.description: Samuel Morse receives his first U.S. Patent (No. 1,647) for the telegraph.

events.title: Alphabetical Code Developed
events.description: Morse develops the 'Alphabetical Code', the direct precursor to Modern Morse Code.

events.title: Telegraph Line Appropriation
events.description: U.S. Congress appropriates $30,000 to build a test line from Washington, D.C. to Baltimore.

events.title: First News Dispatch
events.description: First news dispatch (Whig Party nomination) sent via telegraph from Annapolis Junction.

events.title: What Hath God Wrought!
events.description: Morse sends the official first message: 'What hath God wrought!' from the US Capitol.

events.title: Public Telegraph Office Opens
events.description: The first public telegraph office opens in Washington, D.C.

events.title: Magnetic Telegraph Company
events.description: The Magnetic Telegraph Company is formed to extend lines from D.C. to New York.

events.title: Printing Telegraph Patent
events.description: Royal Earl House patents the first 'Printing Telegraph' which prints letters directly.

events.title: First Telegraphic Arrest
events.description: The first telegraphic arrest occurs in England after a message is sent ahead of a suspect's train.

events.title: Western Union Predecessor Founded
events.description: The New York and Mississippi Valley Printing Telegraph Company (later Western Union) is founded.

events.title: Associated Press (AP) Formed
events.description: The Associated Press is formed to pool telegraph costs for efficient news gathering.

events.title: International Morse Created
events.description: Friedrich Gerke simplifies Morse's code in Germany, creating what became International Morse Code.

events.title: First Telegraphic Election Results
events.description: First telegraphic election results are reported in the race between Taylor and Cass.

events.title: First Submarine Cable
events.description: The first submarine cable is laid across the English Channel; it fails within hours.

events.title: English Channel Success
events.description: The first successful and durable English Channel telegraph cable is completed.

events.title: Telegraph Train Dispatching
events.description: The New York & Erie Railroad becomes the first to use the telegraph for train dispatching.

events.title: Reuters Agency Founded
events.description: Paul Julius Reuter founds the Reuters news agency using telegraphs and carrier pigeons.

events.title: Telegraphic Time Signal
events.description: The first telegraphic time signal is sent from Greenwich Observatory.

events.title: Duplex Telegraphy Invented
events.description: Wilhelm Gintl invents 'Duplex' telegraphy, allowing two messages on one wire simultaneously.

events.title: Transatlantic Project Begins
events.description: Cyrus West Field begins the ambitious project to lay a Transatlantic Cable.

events.title: Improved Printing Telegraph
events.description: David Edward Hughes patents an improved printing telegraph with a piano-style keyboard.

events.title: Name 'Western Union' Adopted
events.description: The name 'Western Union' is officially adopted for the expanding telegraph company.

events.title: First Transatlantic Messages
events.description: First Transatlantic cable completed; Queen Victoria and President Buchanan exchange messages.

events.title: 1858 Cable Fails
events.description: The 1858 cable fails after only three weeks due to insulation breakdown from excessive voltage.

events.title: Pony Express Begins
events.description: The Pony Express begins, though its future is threatened by the advancing telegraph.

events.title: Transcontinental Line Complete
events.description: The first Transcontinental Telegraph line is completed across the United States.

events.title: Pony Express Ceases
events.description: The Pony Express officially ceases operations, rendered obsolete by the transcontinental telegraph.

events.title: Telegraph from a Balloon
events.description: Thaddeus Lowe sends the first telegraph message from a balloon to President Lincoln.

events.title: Military Telegraph Corps
events.description: The U.S. Military Telegraph Corps is formed; Lincoln becomes the first 'telegraphic' president.

events.title: ITU Founded
events.description: The International Telegraph Union (ITU) is founded in Paris to standardize regulations.

events.title: Permanent Transatlantic Cable
events.description: The SS Great Eastern successfully lays the first reliable, permanent Transatlantic cable.

events.title: Stock Exchange Link
events.description: The first telegraphic link between the London and New York Stock Exchanges is established.

events.title: Stock Ticker Invented
events.description: Edward Calahan invents the Stock Ticker, revolutionizing the flow of market data.

events.title: British Nationalization
events.description: The British government nationalizes all private telegraph companies under the Post Office.

events.title: Telegraphic Money Transfer
events.description: Western Union introduces the first telegraphic money transfer service.

events.title: Quadruplex Telegraph
events.description: Thomas Edison invents the 'Quadruplex' telegraph, allowing four messages on one wire.

events.title: Australian Overland Line
events.description: The Australian Overland Telegraph Line is completed, linking Australia to the global network.

events.title: Baudot Code Invented
events.description: Émile Baudot invents the 5-bit 'Baudot Code', the direct ancestor of digital computing.

events.title: Bell Patents Telephone
events.description: Alexander Graham Bell patents the telephone, the first major technology to challenge the telegraph.

events.title: First Telephone Line
events.description: The first commercial telephone line is installed, often using existing telegraph infrastructure.

events.title: Wheatstone Automatic System
events.description: The British Post Office introduces the Wheatstone Automatic system, reaching 400 words per minute.

events.title: Postal Telegraph System
events.description: The Postal Telegraph System is formed to compete with Western Union's monopoly in the US.

events.title: Standard Time Zones adopted
events.description: Standard Time Zones are adopted in the U.S., coordinated via telegraphic time signals.

events.title: Radio Waves Proven
events.description: Heinrich Hertz proves the existence of radio waves, the basis for wireless telegraphy.

events.title: London-Paris Telephone Cable
events.description: The first submarine telephone cable is laid between London and Paris.

events.title: Marconi's Wireless Experiments
events.description: Guglielmo Marconi begins his first wireless telegraphy experiments in Italy.

events.title: Wireless Telegraphy Patent
events.description: Marconi receives the first patent for wireless telegraphy.

events.title: Wireless Telegraph Company
events.description: Marconi establishes the Wireless Telegraph & Signal Company.

events.title: First Wireless Distress Signal
events.description: The first wireless distress signal is sent from the lightship Goodwin Sands.

events.title: Creed System Invented
events.description: Frederick Creed invents the 'Creed System', which converts Morse code directly into text.

events.title: First Transatlantic Wireless
events.description: Marconi sends the first Transatlantic wireless signal (the letter 'S' in Morse).

events.title: All Red Pacific Cable
events.description: The 'All Red' Pacific cable is completed, circling the globe on British territory.

events.title: US-Philippines Cable
events.description: The first Transpacific cable is completed between the U.S. and the Philippines.

events.title: CQD Distress Signal
events.description: CQD is adopted as the first international wireless distress signal.

events.title: Germany Adopts SOS
events.description: Germany adopts 'SOS' as its national distress signal due to its distinct sound.

events.title: SOS Global Standard
events.description: The International Radio Telegraph Convention in Berlin adopts SOS as the global standard.

events.title: SOS Officially Effective
events.description: SOS officially becomes the international standard for distress calls.

events.title: First Major SOS Use
events.description: The first major use of SOS in a real emergency occurs during the wreck of the SS Slavonia.

events.title: ICC Rate Authority
events.description: The Mann-Elkins Act gives the Interstate Commerce Commission authority to regulate telegraph rates.

events.title: World Record Speed Message
events.description: A telegraph message is sent around the world in just 9.5 minutes.

events.title: Sinking of the Titanic
events.description: The sinking of the Titanic; both CQD and SOS are used by wireless operators.

events.title: Radio Act of 1912
events.description: The Radio Act of 1912 mandates 24-hour radio watchkeeping on ships.

events.title: Western Union Multiplexing
events.description: Western Union introduces Multiplexing, allowing 8 messages on a single wire.

events.title: Zimmermann Telegram
events.description: The Zimmermann Telegram is intercepted, helping draw the U.S. into World War I.

events.title: First Telex Service
events.description: The first Telex (teleprinter exchange) service begins in Germany.

events.title: FCC Created
events.description: The Communications Act of 1934 creates the FCC to oversee US telegraphy.

events.title: Western Union Merger
events.description: Western Union merges with its last major rival, Postal Telegraph, becoming a monopoly.

events.title: WWII Code Breaking
events.description: Morse code remains the primary medium for intercepting and decoding wartime signals.

events.title: Moscow-Washington Hotline
events.description: The Moscow-Washington 'Hotline' is established using teletype technology.

events.title: World Wide Web Public
events.description: The World Wide Web becomes public, signaling the final end of the Wired World.

events.title: Maritime Morse Requirement Ends
events.description: International maritime regulations officially end the requirement for Morse code.

events.title: Final Western Union Telegram
events.description: Western Union sends its final telegram, ending 155 years of service on Jan 27.

events.title: India Shuts Down Telegraph
events.description: India's state-run BSNL shuts down the world's last major commercial telegraph system.

events.title: Modern Morse Usage
events.description: Morse code remains a vital skill for amateur radio operators and a symbol of communications history.
